objectives: Recognise a quadratic equation and write it in the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0.
Solve a quadratic equation by splitting the middle term.
Derive and apply the quadratic formula.
Decide the nature of the roots from the discriminant without solving.
Model a word problem as a quadratic equation and interpret both roots.

blocks.title: Hook question
blocks.summary: A rectangular garden is 3 m longer than it is wide and covers 40 m². How wide is it? Let pupils guess and check before any algebra.
steps: Pose the question and take three quick answers.
Write the predictions on the board to revisit at the end.

blocks.title: Teach: What makes an equation quadratic
blocks.summary: A quadratic equation has degree two: ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. Rewrite each situation in standard form before trying to solve it.
steps: Model it: The garden gives x(x + 3) = 40, so x² + 3x − 40 = 0.
Pause for two checking questions before going on.
Pupils copy the key statement in their own words.

blocks.title: Group task
blocks.summary: In pairs, sort eight equations into quadratic and not quadratic, rewriting each quadratic one in standard form.
steps: Groups of four, roles assigned: reader, recorder, checker, reporter.
Circulate and ask each group one why question.

blocks.title: Exit questions
blocks.summary: Three short questions; collect answers to plan the next lesson.
steps: Is (x − 2)² = x² + 4 a quadratic equation?
Write x(2x + 1) = 6 in standard form.
Why must a be non-zero?

blocks.title: Practice from the textbook
blocks.summary: Exercise 4.1, questions 1 and 2: decide which are quadratic and frame the word problems.

periods.focus: Solving by splitting the middle term

blocks.title: Hook question
blocks.summary: Find two numbers whose product is −40 and whose sum is 3. Race the board.
steps: Pose the question and take three quick answers.
Write the predictions on the board to revisit at the end.

blocks.title: Teach: Solving by splitting the middle term
blocks.summary: Split bx into two terms whose coefficients multiply to ac, factorise by grouping, then set each factor to zero.
steps: Model it: x² + 3x − 40 = (x + 8)(x − 5) = 0, so x = 5 m for the garden; −8 is rejected as a width.
Pause for two checking questions before going on.
Pupils copy the key statement in their own words.

blocks.title: Group task
blocks.summary: Factor relay: each row of pupils passes one step of a factorisation forward; the last pupil checks the roots by substitution.
steps: Groups of four, roles assigned: reader, recorder, checker, reporter.
Circulate and ask each group one why question.

blocks.title: Exit questions
blocks.summary: Three short questions; collect answers to plan the next lesson.
steps: Factorise 2x² − 7x + 3.
Solve 6x² − x − 2 = 0.
Why is one root of the garden problem rejected?

blocks.title: Practice from the textbook
blocks.summary: Exercise 4.2, questions 1 (iii) to (vi) and 4.
